rationale:
The reviewed test adequately checks `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions.content`.

The subject is checked by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. The requirement has four content obligations. The test covers each one:

1. **Call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting.** The test takes `instructions` from the first, empty `search_text` result. It asserts that the string contains "Before submitting, close every delivered search page" and "finish_search".
2. **Select the tags of excerpts used as evidence.** It asserts the phrase "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read".
3. **Pass `used: []` when none contributed.** It asserts the phrase "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result". The test's use of an empty result also fits the case where no excerpt contributed.
4. **Finishing records the selected inputs without fetching more source.** It asserts the phrase "without reading more source". It also exercises `finish_search`, checking that the returned dependencies contain the selected node with its fingerprint. A finish with `used: []` returns no dependencies. `tools.domain.0.lock().unwrap().reads` stays 0, so finishing did not fetch more source.

The test also checks that a `search_structure` result delivered to a fresh session carries the same `instructions` string as the `search_text` one. That means both search kinds supply the content. Several more assertions cover the delivery rule, which the parent requirement `first_search.instructions` owns. Later searches omit the field, continuation pages omit it, and it is present even when `matches` is empty.

The assertions are substring checks, not an exact-text comparison. That is a sound way to enforce the content requirement, because the text does not fix an exact wording. I found no plausible content omission the assertions would accept. For example, instructions that left out the `used: []` guidance or the "no more source" statement would fail. I found no gaps and no marking gaps, since the test carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
